description: Network Rail, which manages the railway infrastructure of Great Britain, has had a Weather Resilience and Climate Change Adaptation (WRCCA) strategy since 2017 and aims to have prepared the infrastructure to minimise climate impacts by 2050. Its pages say heavy rain floods tracks and causes landslips needing months of repair, and that the company reports to Defra every five years under the Adaptation Reporting Power of the Climate Change Act 2008; the Fourth Adaptation Report (December 2024) has an Integrated Climate Change Risk Assessment as appendix A. Its five regions produced WRCCA plans for 2024 to 2029 that identify asset risks and guide investment in Control Period 7; they were issued to the Office of Rail and Road with the CP7 Delivery Plan in March 2024 and align with the DfT transport adaptation consultation of April 2024. Coverage: the British rail network by region. Format and access: free PDF reports and plans. Licence and cost: free to read; no reuse licence is stated. Caveats: the plans are summaries of internal risk work, not datasets. It supports climate adaptation, resilience and hazard exposure studies of rail assets. It relates to the Network Rail drainage allowances case, Network Rail open data feeds and the Carmont derailment investigation in the catalogue.
